caveats: Boundaries for 430 official districts were obtained from ARAZI. Temporary district boundaries were digitized from maps published by GSIA in their annual population estimates (2025-2026). These may not be very accurate due to the resolution of the source maps. The list of 457 districts was obtained from the Ministry of Internal Affairs (MoI), via Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MoFA).
dataset_source: Afghanistan Land Authority (ARAZI), General Statistics and Information Authority (GSIA)
license_title: Creative Commons Attribution for Intergovernmental Organisations (CC BY-IGO)
methodology_other:
Dataset: Government survey  
  
P-codes: National system adapted to OCHA standards, in some cases, pcodes from previous version was retained for backwards compatibility. Original pcodes from the data sources (adjusted to OCHA standards), and the old p-codes are included for reference.
name: cod-ab-afg
notes:
Afghanistan administrative level 0-2 boundaries (COD-AB) dataset version 04.  
  
This dataset is structured into 2 levels:  
- Admin 1: 34 Province  
- Admin 2: 457 District  
  
  
Dates associated with this dataset:  
- 23 June 2026: dataset reviewed for accuracy and completeness  
- 26 July 2026: valid for use by the humanitarian community  
- 23 June 2026: last edit to the dataset before publishing  
- 01 June 2026: boundaries created by the source  
  
Contributed by [OCHA Afghanistan](https://data.humdata.org/organization/ocha-afghanistan).  
Quality assured, configured, and published by [OCHA Field Information Services (FIS)](https://data.humdata.org/organization/ocha-fiss) and [HDX](https://data.humdata.org/organization/hdx).  
  
Part of the dataset: [Global Subnational Administrative Boundaries](https://data.humdata.org/dataset/cod-ab-global)
